what_its_for: This medicine is a hormone used to treat several conditions. In women, it helps trigger the release of an egg from the ovary (ovulation) and is often used as part of fertility treatments. In men and boys, it is used to treat a condition where the testicles have not dropped into the scrotum (undescended testicles) and to help with low testosterone caused by a hormone problem. Your doctor will explain exactly why you are taking it.
how_to_take: This medicine is given as a shot (injection) under the skin or into a muscle. A healthcare provider may give you the injection in a clinic or doctor's office. In some cases, you or a caregiver may be taught how to give the injection at home. If you are injecting at home, always follow the exact instructions your doctor or nurse taught you. Use a new needle and syringe each time. Never share your needles or medicine with anyone else. Mix the powder with the liquid provided only when you are ready to use it, and throw away any unused mixed medicine.
dosing: Your dose and how often you take this medicine depends on what it is being used to treat, your age, and your body weight. Your doctor will tell you exactly how much to use and how often. Do not change your dose on your own. Common schedules may involve one or more injections per week or a single injection at a specific time during a fertility treatment cycle. Always follow your doctor's personalized instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or fertility clinic right away for instructions — especially if you are using this medicine as part of a timed fertility treatment, since the timing of the injection can be very important. Do not double up on doses without talking to your doctor first.
storage: Store unmixed powder vials at room temperature, away from heat and direct sunlight. After mixing the powder with liquid, store in the refrigerator and use within the time frame listed on the label (usually within 30 to 60 days, depending on the brand). The prefilled Ovidrel syringe should be stored in the refrigerator but can be kept at room temperature for up to 30 days. Keep all medicines away from children and pets. Do not freeze. Throw away any medicine that has changed color, looks cloudy, or has particles floating in it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid smoking and drinking alcohol, as these can reduce the effectiveness of fertility treatments and harm your health. Do not start any new prescription or over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, or herbal supplements without first checking with your doctor. If you are using this medicine for fertility, avoid unprotected sex unless your doctor has told you it is okay, since multiple eggs may be released and the chance of twins or more is higher. Avoid activities that cause pelvic pain or discomfort, and tell your doctor right away if you feel bloated or have stomach pain.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you have: severe pain or bloating in your stomach or pelvis, sudden weight gain of more than 5 pounds in a day, nausea or vomiting that will not stop, difficulty breathing or shortness of breath, decreased urination, swelling in your hands or legs, or signs of a blood clot such as pain, redness, or swelling in your leg, chest pain, or trouble breathing. Also call your doctor if you notice signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, rash, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing. In boys, call the doctor if you notice early signs of puberty such as pubic hair growth, deepening of the voice, or acne.
when_it_works: For women using this medicine to trigger ovulation, the egg is usually released within 36 to 48 hours after the injection. Pregnancy testing is typically done about two weeks after the injection if you are undergoing fertility treatment. For boys or men, improvements such as testicle descent or changes in hormone levels may take several weeks to months of treatment. Your doctor will monitor your progress with blood tests or ultrasounds.
special_populations: Pregnancy: This medicine is used to help achieve pregnancy, but once you are pregnant it should not be used unless specifically directed by your doctor. Breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are breastfeeding. Children: This medicine is sometimes used in boys for undescended testicles, but it must be closely monitored by a doctor because it can cause early signs of puberty. Elderly: This medicine is not commonly used in elderly patients. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have any kidney or liver problems, as dose adjustments may be needed.
